notes:
The CEQA documents list the project scope as PM5.6 to PM12.1 (Ophir Rd), but the spreadsheet says 5.6 to 9.1 (Palermo/Welsh Rd). Looking at Google Earth, it looks like the actual project scope is closer to 9.1 (might actually be closer to 9.3). Furthermore, because the spreadsheet lists the project as one entry, it is difficult to split the lane miles information in each direct. The spreadsheet describes 2.6 lane miles of left-turn pockets and 6.2 lane miles of general-purpose lanes. While the majority of the length of the project had only one lane in each direction, there were stretches at the beginning and the end where there was asymmetry on each side. Thus, adjudicating how much of the general-purpose lane mileage added was in each direction becomes quite difficult. Example photos in the 2-pager. 

There are no PEMS stations for SR70 in Butte County, so Traffic Census counts were used instead. The traffic counts are separated by direction (ahead referring to eastbound traffic, back referring to westbound traffic), however there is no indication how the two-way left-turn lane is handled.
